summary: Nicaragua’s restoration agenda is led by a 2030 goal to increase forest cover by 21.47%, alongside 1,425,935 ha of natural regeneration in protected/recovered areas—about 19.7% of the country’s current 7,235,100 ha forest cover—and 1,166,362 ha of degraded land to be improved. It also reports more than 47,000 ha of annual forest recovery since 2007 and a 2024–2029 plan to establish 99.3 million plants. Conservation combines a conditional 25% reduction in gross-deforestation emissions by 2030 from the national baseline with 104,000 ha of pine monitoring, 25,000 ha of soil-and-water works, and protection of 363 springs. Mixed restoration/management measures include 2.8 million ha under the 20x20 objective, recovery of 1,110,721 ha degraded land, and 6,464 linear km of windbreaks. Agriculture targets 555,361 ha of agroforestry—13.7% of current agricultural area—plus 416,520 ha of timber plantations and 277,680 ha supporting sustainable agricultural businesses.
